questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: New pop groups with strange names
New vegetables made by mixing two different plants
How to cook traditional British vegetables
Why British people don't eat vegetables
questions.why: They discuss new hybrid vegetables and the people who grow, cook and eat them.

questions.q: What did Sam first think Kalettes and CauliShoots were?
options: Names of pop groups
Types of fruit
Restaurants
Cooking tools
questions.why: Sam says they sound like the names of pop groups.

questions.q: What two vegetables were mixed to create the Kalette?
options: Broccoli and Chinese kale
Cauliflower and carrots
Kale and Brussels sprouts
Leeks and potatoes
questions.why: Sam says the Kalette is a mix between kale and a Brussels sprout.

questions.q: How were Kalettes advertised when they were introduced in 2010?
options: As a cheap vegetable for soups and stews
As a fun vegetable for young children
As a luxury food for expensive restaurants
As a healthy vegetable, cooked or raw
questions.why: They were advertised as a healthy vegetable that could be cooked or eaten raw.

questions.q: How does Jamie Claxton describe the way he created the Kalette?
options: By trying wacky ideas to see what happened
By following a plan suggested by customers
By copying a vegetable grown in China
By using chemicals to change the plant's genes
questions.why: He says they 'just try wacky stuff and see what happens'.

questions.q: Why did Jamie want to create something new?
options: Brussels sprouts were becoming too expensive
Sprouts and kale felt old-fashioned
Farmers asked him for bigger vegetables
Kale didn't grow well in the cold UK weather
questions.why: He says they needed something more modern because sprouts and kale are very traditional.

questions.q: According to Jack Stein, what matters most when choosing new vegetables?
options: The price that customers are willing to pay
How long they last in the fridge
Their taste and how they look on the plate
Where they are grown and how far they travel
questions.why: He says it's down to taste and what it looks like on the plate.

questions.q: Why does Jack Stein mention the old name 'Flower Sprouts'?
options: To say it was a much better name than Kalettes
To complain that the new name is confusing
To show that the vegetable was never popular
To give an example of novelty he likes
questions.why: He mentions novelty, saying things like Kalettes, originally 'Flower Sprouts', were great.
